prompt: If I randomly select i.i.d. samples from a distribution n times, the distribution of the sampled variables will approximately follow a normal distribution as n becomes very large. This statement is based on which theory?
answer:
This is based on the **Central Limit Theorem (CLT)**.

More precisely, if \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are i.i.d. with finite mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\sigma^2\), then as \(n\) becomes large,

\[
\frac{\sqrt n(\bar X_n-\mu)}{\sigma}
\;\xrightarrow{d}\;
N(0,1),
\]

so the **sample mean** is approximately

\[
\bar X_n \sim N\left(\mu,\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right).
\]

The CLT applies to the **sum or average** of the sampled variables—not generally to the individual raw observations themselves. The latter continue to follow the original distribution.
